justification: The capacity engine drives the user-facing yield (GFA and dwellings) on the Verify and Brief surfaces. Two defects made it return null or wrong yield for DCP-only councils: it read height from the LEP only and ignored the structured DCP max_height, and the landscaping step subtracted the required open space from an already coverage-capped footprint, driving it to zero. Both are silent-wrong-number risks on a compliance surface, so they need golden coverage and explicit provenance for a DCP-sourced height.

pre_impl.existing_data: The structured DCP already carries max_height for 8 of 28 councils (including Wingecarribee) and max_site_coverage and landscaping_min for most, verified live via /api/dcp/structured-controls; the engine consumed setbacks, site coverage and landscaping from the DCP but took height only from the LEP planning-controls field.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Confirmed against the live production brief for 38 Park Road Bowral: lep_height and lep_fsr both null and realistic_gfa null at low confidence, while the council DCP publishes a max_height — proving the yield collapsed from a wiring gap, not only absent data.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new capability; reuses the existing _get_dcp_value helper to read the DCP max_height as a fallback and keeps lep_height_m honest as None, and corrects the landscaping step to cap the footprint at lot-minus-open-space rather than subtracting from the reduced footprint.

functions.name: compute_constraint_arithmetic
functions.input: lot area, dev type, optional LEP height and FSR strings, DCP controls, SEPP standards and overrides, and shadow result
functions.output: a constraint-arithmetic result whose height envelope now falls back to the DCP max_height and whose footprint is capped rather than zeroed by landscaping
functions.if_none: when neither the LEP nor the DCP supplies a height, the height envelope stays unavailable and a single explicit gap records that both sources were empty

values.read_at: compute_constraint_arithmetic seeds the envelope height from the DCP only when the LEP maps no height for this lot
values.if_missing: a None DCP height leaves the base height None and the height envelope is skipped with a recorded gap rather than a guessed value

break_it.scenario: A regional lot has no LEP height or FSR but the council DCP publishes a max_height, as on the Bowral flag lot
break_it.what_happens: the pre-fix engine read only the LEP height, found none, and returned a null yield for the whole DCP-only council
break_it.how: the engine now falls back to the structured DCP max_height, computes storeys, and records that the height was taken from the DCP for verification
break_it.repro: run the new TestDcpHeightFallbackRegional case with lep_height None and a DCP max_height and confirm storeys and a non-null GFA

break_it.scenario: A lot has a 25 percent site-coverage cap and a 75 percent landscaping requirement describing the same lot partition
break_it.what_happens: subtracting the 3072 square metre landscaping from the already coverage-capped 1024 square metre footprint drove the buildable footprint to zero and the yield to nothing
break_it.how: landscaping now caps the footprint at lot area minus required open space and takes the minimum with the current footprint, so a build and its landscaping that both fit are not double-counted
break_it.repro: assert the landscaping step footprint stays 1024 square metres on the 4096 square metre Bowral-style lot rather than collapsing to zero

break_it.scenario: A DCP-sourced height is presented to the reader as though it were the LEP height
break_it.what_happens: an unlabelled fallback would misstate the provenance of the height a planner is relying on for the envelope
break_it.how: lep_height_m stays None because the LEP genuinely has none, and a gap explicitly states the height was taken from the council DCP and should be verified against it
break_it.repro: check that lep_height_m is None and a gap contains taken from the council DCP after the fallback fires

post_merge.manual_verify: 205 capacity and constraint tests pass including the new regional fallback class; the two capacity golden scenarios changed only the height-gap wording (no numeric drift, diff eyeballed) and the Inner West golden corrected the landscaping double-count from 360 to 450. Live re-verification against the Bowral brief needs the Railway deploy after merge; the DCP height value itself is data-quality, not this change.
